entry.title: How Lua obfuscation actually works - and what it can and can't protect
entry.summary: If you ship Lua scripts - Roblox games, game mods, embedded logic - your source That's the problem obfuscation exists to mitigate. Here's how it actually On Roblox specifically, executors and script dumpers can capture source or Your game logic, formulas, and tuning constants Remote event names and call patterns (which helps exploit writers) API keys or endpoints you forgot to keep server-side Hours of design work, ready to copy-paste into someone else's game Minification. Strips whitespace, renames locals. Fast, tiny output, and it String encryption. Literals are stored encrypted and decrypted at runtime. strings pass - Control-flow flattening. The linear structure of the code is replaced by a Bytecode/VM-level transforms. The script is compiled to a custom bytecode and the slowest, since you're paying an interpreter tax at runtime. No client-side obfuscation is a guarantee. Given enough time, anything running Obfuscation raises the cost of theft from minutes to hours. Most theft is The things that matter most still don't belong in the client: Anti-cheat decisions should be validated server-side Secrets and keys should never ship to the client at all Trust-critical state changes belong on the server, always Keep real secrets server-side. Obfuscation is not a substitute. Obfuscate the client scripts that contain logic worth protecting. Verify the output still runs on Roblox and on the executors your users actually use - broken obfuscation is worse than none. Keep the unobfuscated source in version control (you'll thank yourself). I built Obrion - a free browser-based Lua/Luau guides covering the threat model in Obfuscation is defense-in-depth: it won't stop a determined reverse engineer, but it reliably stops the copy-paste majority - and for most Roblox devs, that's the threat that actually costs them.

entry.summary:

I've been working on a personal learning project called Building LLM Technologies, where I explore individual components of language models using small Python notebooks. entry.title: My Final year project Writing
entry.summary: Nobody really tells you what it takes to write a final-year research project. 🎓 When I started my Mathematics and Statistics project on Modelling Queuing Systems and Customer Wait Times Using Markov Chains and Simulation, I thought the hardest part would be the mathematics. I soon realised that research goes beyond equations, calculations, and writing chapters. One of my biggest lessons? You cannot force your data to support a conclusion simply because it fits your original plan. I also learned that AI tools can help with research and writing, but you must still verify the information, understand your analysis, and take responsibility for your work. A good research project is not just about submitting five chapters. It is about understanding the problem, explaining your findings, acknowledging limitations, and defending your decisions. I'm still learning, but the process is teaching me patience, critical thinking, and intellectual honesty. To every final-year student: keep going. Research is a process of learning, questioning, and improving. For those who have completed their projects, what was the biggest lesson you learned?
